source_locators: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, Version 5 (11 January 2019), held PDF, p. 244 (definition of uniform integrability; the bound sup E|X_i| <= M+1; the dominated example)
components.gap: Supply on the route this entry's source variant of the definition: Durrett defines uniform integrability for an arbitrary collection of random variables X_i, i in I, with no integrability hypothesis (the limit as M tends to infinity of sup_i E(|X_i|;|X_i|>M) is zero), and remarks that a choice of M making the supremum less than one gives sup_i E|X_i| <= M+1, so integrability of every member is a consequence of the condition rather than a hypothesis and a collection containing a variable of infinite mean is not uniformly integrable (v5 p. 244). The route's def:p15-uniform-integrability (body lines 15-35) defines the notion only for families of real integrable random variables, a narrowed variant of the source definition; the M+1 bound appears on the route only as a step inside the integrable-family proof (annex lines 6-7). Text supplying the source form exists only in the unrouted owner file handbook/parts/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-014.tex lines 554-597 with its proof at handbook/annex/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-014.tex lines 466-503 (owned by w02c-p15-014; route pending).

source_locators: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, Version 5 (11 January 2019), held PDF, p. 245 (Theorem 4.6.2, its examples and proof; the sentence presenting it as a common way to check uniform integrability)
components.gap: Supply on the route Durrett's Theorem 4.6.2 in its source form (v5 p. 245): for real random variables X_i with no integrability assumed and any function phi >= 0 with phi(x)/x tending to infinity (examples x^p with p > 1 and x log+ x), a bound E phi(|X_i|) <= C for all i implies uniform integrability, with the integrability of each X_i derived from the moment bound; and his statement that this is a common way to check uniform integrability. The route's thm:p15-ui-moment-criteria (body lines 48-61; proof annex lines 34-74) is stated for the integrable families of def:p15-uniform-integrability, and its proof (annex lines 36-44) never derives integrability of the X_i, so the source's hypothesis-free form is replaced by a narrowed variant carrying an unstated integrability assumption; the 'common way' statement is absent. Text supplying the source form exists only in the unrouted owner file handbook/parts/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-014.tex lines 599-634 with its proof at handbook/annex/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-014.tex lines 505-549 (owned by w02c-p15-014; route pending). components.gap: Supply on the route the source's continuation of Theorem 4.6.9, Levy's 0-1 law (v5 pp. 247-248), in full: the challenge Durrett borrows from Chung to judge whether the law is obvious or incredible; the obvious reading (the indicator of A is F_infinity-measurable and F_n increases to F_infinity, so the best prediction of the indicator from F_n should approach the best prediction from F_infinity, which is the indicator itself); the incredible reading that yields Kolmogorov's 0-1 law (present on the route); and Durrett's closing evaluation that the tail argument may not show the result to be incredible but that it and later applications show the theorem to be very useful. The route's thm:p15-levy-information-law (body lines 161-176; annex lines 287-305) gives the theorem, its proof and the Kolmogorov derivation only; the Chung challenge, the obvious reading as an interpretation and the evaluation are absent, and the source's name Levy's 0-1 law appears only as an index entry (body line 175). source_locators: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, Version 5 (11 January 2019), held PDF, p. 248 (Exercise 4.6.1, with its statistical reading and the definitions of prior and posterior distribution)
components.gap: Supply on the route this entry's definitions and statistical reading from Durrett's Exercise 4.6.1 (v5 p. 248): the prior distribution is the law of theta; the posterior distribution after n observations is P(theta in . | Y_1,...,Y_n), so that E(theta|Y_1,...,Y_n) is the posterior mean; and when the Z_i are normal(0,1) the observations are a sample from a normal population with variance 1 and unknown mean. The route's thm:p15-posterior-mean-consistency (body lines 256-270; annex lines 458-479) proves the convergence (a.s. and in L1) but uses the words prior variable and posterior consistency without defining the prior or the posterior distribution, never identifies E(theta|F_n) as a posterior mean, and mentions only independent normal (0,1) noise without the population reading. Annex line 44 says this proves the source criterion, but the route's criterion is the integrable-family variant (see the C003 gap). The source's proof device eps_M = sup{x/phi(x): x >= M} is replaced by the equivalent choice of M_eps.

C004 (annex lines 76-99): the small-event bound for |X| is taken from the tail-splitting theorem rather than from the source's dominated-convergence-and-contradiction step; the source's main device (conditional Jensen and Chebyshev with an absolute-continuity delta) is retained.
C012: no index entry on the route names any dominated convergence theorem, conditional or not.
C015 (body line 253) states that the theorem gives the complete source Exercises 4.6.2-3, while the remark ending Exercise 4.6.3 is missing on the route (see the C015 gap).
C016 (annex line 460): the strong law used is not cross-referenced by label, although the route proves it (thm:p15-iid-series-strong-law, thm:p15-etemadi-strong-law).

C021 (body lines 351-353; annex lines 633-641): the vector extension is asserted for all preceding upward and downward conditional limits, while the proof names only the scalar upward and downward theorems; the coordinatewise argument is generic.
